title: Move the posts API onto a Resource
summary: Returning the model leaks the author's email. Move it onto a JsonResource and handle the relation with whenLoaded.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers\Api;

use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use App\Models\Post;

class PostController extends Controller
{
    public function index()
    {
        return Post::with('author')->latest()->paginate(20);
    }

    public function show(Post $post)
    {
        return $post->load('author');
    }
}

turns.user: /api/posts is returning the author's email and is_admin. and draft_note on the post. only send what we need

assistant.body: Sure! Returning the model turns every column that is not in $hidden into JSON. An API Resource lets you list the fields that go out explicitly. Let's make one for Post and one for User.
php artisan make:resource PostResource && php artisan make:resource UserResource
The Resource is now the single source of truth for the response shape. author is only included when it has been loaded, so relations are handled robustly too.

turns.user: they said the list doesnt need author so I dropped with('author') and now it runs 22 queries. why

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. $this->author lazy loads the moment you touch the property, so it goes back for the author once per post, 20 times. whenLoaded('author') drops the key from the output when the relation was not loaded. In other words, the query decides what goes out.

turns.user: ok now they want the name back on the list. sorry for the back and forth

assistant.body: Only the list query changes: with('author') goes back in. The Resource stays on whenLoaded, so it is left alone, and the query count no longer grows with the number of posts.
